result.summary: Annotates CBlockIndex's nTx and m_chain_tx_count fields with GUARDED_BY(cs_main) and adds required lock enforcement. This prevents data races when RPCs access block index metadata concurrently with block data processing.
result.problem: Reads of CBlockIndex::nTx in getblockheader and m_chain_tx_count in getchaintxstats can race against writes during block receipt, pruned block redownloading, or assumeutxo background validation because the cs_main locking requirement was never documented or enforced by thread safety annotations.
evidence: PR description: 'reading nTx from the getblockheader RPC may race as it does not acquire cs_main. Also, m_chain_tx_count may race in getchaintxstats if a pruned node redownloads a block via getblockfrompeer or if the node is running assumeutxo and tries to read m_chain_tx_count while it is being written to.'
result.scope_notes: Small thread safety annotation update spanning block index definitions and calling RPCs.
result.card: Adds GUARDED_BY(cs_main) annotations to CBlockIndex fields nTx and m_chain_tx_count to resolve data races. Currently, getblockheader reads nTx without holding cs_main while block data is being received, and getchaintxstats can race on m_chain_tx_count during assumeutxo validation or block redownloads on pruned nodes. The author identifies explicit RPC and background thread concurrency bugs that the locking annotation prevents.
uncertainties: Diff is not available in the prompt, so specific lock acquisition sites in RPC callers cannot be directly inspected.

risk.why: Locking mistakes or missing locks around cs_main could induce deadlocks or performance regressions across validation and RPC threads.
